## Final report

**Prior record's lightest PASS design:** 10 mm graphite, 18 kg/m² (screen 403 K, FE hotspot 325 K, mass 18 kg/m², thickness 1 cm — all pass).

**Key finding from the brief that shaped my whole approach:** the FE hotspot (R2, the only requirement with any real margin pressure) was essentially *flat with thickness* for every pure material tested — graphite held at 325 K across 10/20/30 mm, aluminium at 324 K, copper at 322 K. Meanwhile, layering just 2 mm of copper onto a 10 mm aluminium base already captured copper's full spreading benefit (324→323 K), and adding a 3rd or 5th mm of copper added nothing further. Together these say the hotspot is governed by a near-surface spreading effect that saturates within a few millimetres, not by the total plate thickness — so 10 mm is very likely far more material than is needed, and R1/R3/R4 have so much slack (even at low thickness) that they're never at risk.

**Submitted set (10 candidates, graphite as the primary material since it's the lightest usable conductor: k=150 W/mK, ρ=1800 kg/m³, clearly better mass-for-performance than aluminium or copper):**

| candidate | design | mass (kg/m²) |
|---|---|---|
| c-0000 | 10 mm graphite | 18.0 (safe anchor, exact prior match) |
| c-0001 | 8 mm graphite | 14.4 |
| c-0002 | 6 mm graphite | 10.8 |
| c-0003 | 5 mm graphite | 9.0 |
| c-0004 | 4 mm graphite | 7.2 |
| c-0005 | 3 mm graphite | 5.4 |
| c-0006 | 2 mm graphite | 3.6 |
| c-0007 | 1 mm copper + 2 mm graphite | 12.56 |
| c-0008 | 1 mm copper + 3 mm graphite | 14.36 |
| c-0009 | 2 mm copper + 3 mm graphite | 23.32 |

The pure-graphite thicknesses form a graduated bet from validated-safe (10 mm) down to my boldest extrapolation (2 mm), all reasoned from the observed saturation behavior. The three copper-faced hybrids are insurance: copper gives superior near-surface spreading at a known-good 1–2 mm cladding depth (replicating the prior sweep's copper-on-aluminium data), in case pure thin graphite alone can't spread adequately at very low thickness.

**Lightest candidate I believe meets every requirement:** c-0006 (2 mm pure graphite, 3.6 kg/m²) — this carries the least supporting margin of the set and is a genuine extrapolation beyond any tested data point, but it's directly motivated by the fast-saturation evidence from the copper-cladding data, and R1/R3/R4 are nowhere close to binding at that thickness.

No further action needed — submission and finish are complete; there's no opportunity to revise.
